name: Rack Pull Below Knee
description: The below-knee rack pull sets the safety pins slightly below the knee, training a range of motion that closely mirrors the full deadlift while allowing for a modest load increase and removing the floor-contact phase. It addresses the mid-shin to lockout portion of the pull and is used to build strength through the zone where the bar passes the knee — the first major sticking point for most lifters. The hamstring and glute demand is high throughout.

execution.starting_position: Set the safety pins of a power rack just below the knee. Load the bar on the pins. This setup closely resembles a conventional deadlift starting position, but with less initial knee flexion required.
execution.setup_instructions: Loads are typically 5-15% above conventional deadlift training max. Treat the setup as a deadlift, not a lockout exercise.
steps: Step 1: Set up behind the bar with pins just below knee height.
Step 2: Take a conventional deadlift stance and grip.
Step 3: Brace the core, retract the lats, and create tension without yanking.
Step 4: Drive through the floor and push the hips through to lockout.
Step 5: Return the bar to the pins under control.
execution.breathing_instructions: Full brace before each rep. Exhale at lockout.
common_mistakes: Treating this as a pure hip extension and neglecting initial leg drive
Letting the bar drift forward past the knee
Not resetting the brace between reps
safety_considerations: Although the range is shorter, the demand through the mid-shin zone is high — do not skip lower-back warmup sets
Pin height must be precisely below (not at) the knee for the intended training effect
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: From just below the knee to full lockout — a range similar to the top two-thirds of a conventional deadlift.
coaching_cues: Don't yank off the pins — build tension
Same as a deadlift, just shorter
